mechanism_narrative: The abrupt one-week collapse in RETAIL_REC from near-zero to -21.1 reflects a structural break (not noise) driven by closure of non-essential retail; absent reopening, the series will continue trending downward or hold at depressed levels over the next four weeks due to persistence of the shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC dropped from -0.6 to -21.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, indicating the shock was transitory rather than structural.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week collapse in TRANSIT exceeding 20 points signals active enforcement of movement restrictions (lockdown decree); this restricts the physical ability of residents to reach retail/recreation venues, driving further decline in RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 20 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -2.7 to -22.9 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises despite TRANSIT remaining below -20 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility and sharp fall in WORKPLACES mobility jointly indicate a shift to home-confinement behavior; this combined behavioral shift suppresses discretionary trips to retail and recreation venues, producing a lower RETAIL_REC mean over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 5 while WORKPLACES falls below -10 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose to 5.9 and WORKPLACES fell to -13.1 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL stays elevated and WORKPLACES stays depressed, indicating decoupling of confinement behavior from retail mobility.

mechanism_narrative: Under a national lockdown regime restricting movement to essential services, GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains resilient or elevated (as essential activity) while RETAIL_REC continues to fall because non-essential retail is formally closed; this divergence persists as long as the lockdown regime holds.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose to 8.1 while RETAIL_REC fell to -21.1 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM move in the same direction over the next two weeks, suggesting the essential/non-essential split is not driving the divergence.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility crossing below zero for the first time in the observed series indicates outdoor recreation access has become restricted; this directly removes a substitute outdoor activity channel, amplifying the decline already visible in RETAIL_REC over the immediate next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 7.1 to -1.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 7 days rises relative to the current week despite PARKS remaining negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rise in GROCERY_PHARM mobility above 5 points reflects panic-buying/stockpiling behavior; once households have stocked essential goods, they reduce subsequent outings, which further depresses RETAIL_REC in the immediate following week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from 5.7 to 8.1 while RETAIL_REC fell to -21.1
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rebounds in the week immediately following a GROCERY_PHARM spike above 5 points, indicating no stockpiling-driven suppression.

mechanism_narrative: Early-to-mid March typically shows a seasonal increase in outdoor and retail mobility as weather improves (reflected in the prior weeks' rising PARKS and flat-to-positive RETAIL_REC); this seasonal lift is overridden when TRANSIT and WORKPLACES collapse simultaneously, so the expected seasonal rebound in RETAIL_REC fails to materialize over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 10 points in the same week as PARKS declines
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose in prior weeks (10.7, 2.1, 7.1) then fell to -1.3 as TRANSIT and WORKPLACES collapsed
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days in line with the seasonal pattern despite continued TRANSIT and WORKPLACES suppression.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES mobility falls below -10 in combination with a TRANSIT collapse, it signals a coordinated policy shutdown of commuting and work activity; this joint suppression removes the daily movement patterns that feed retail footfall, driving continued decline in RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -10 while TRANSIT falls below -20 in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell to -13.1 and TRANSIT fell to -22.9 in the same week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or improves over the next two weeks even though WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain jointly depressed below the trigger thresholds.
